about:
# Turkey Tickle UI

A suite of UI addons for **World of Warcraft: Forever**. Each module is its own addon, so you can
enable only the ones you want.

| Module | Folder | Description |
| ------ | ------ | ----------- |
| [Plates](https://github.com/TurkeyTickle/TurkeyTickleUI/blob/main/TurkeyTickleUI_Plates) | `TurkeyTickleUI_Plates` | Blizzard-style nameplates with threat warnings, cast bars and debuffs |
| [Pets](https://github.com/TurkeyTickle/TurkeyTickleUI/blob/main/TurkeyTickleUI_Pets) | `TurkeyTickleUI_Pets` | Hunter pet guide: where to learn pet skills, what to tame, rare pets on the map |
| [Puzzle](https://github.com/TurkeyTickle/TurkeyTickleUI/blob/main/TurkeyTickleUI_Puzzle) | `TurkeyTickleUI_Puzzle` | Multiplayer jigsaw puzzles: host a picture, solve it together with your guild or group |
| [Cooking](https://github.com/TurkeyTickle/TurkeyTickleUI/blob/main/TurkeyTickleUI_Cooking) | `TurkeyTickleUI_Cooking` | Cooking coach: what in your bags levels Cooking, reminders to cook it, mobs nearby to hunt |
| [XP](https://github.com/TurkeyTickle/TurkeyTickleUI/blob/main/TurkeyTickleUI_XP) | `TurkeyTickleUI_XP` | A tiny movable XP/hour window with session average, trend line and time to level |

## Install

Download the zip from the latest [GitHub release](https://github.com/TurkeyTickle/TurkeyTickleUI/releases)
and extract it into `World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns/`. `TurkeyTickleUI-<version>`
has every module; `TurkeyTickleUI_Puzzle-<version>` is the Puzzle module on its own.

To run straight from the repository instead, copy (or symlink) each module folder into:

```
World of Warcraft/_forever_/Interface/AddOns/
```

To develop next to a release install, run `tools/dev_link.sh [AddOns folder]` instead. It links
`TurkeyTickleUI_<Module>_Dev` copies of the repository that show up as a separate **[DEV]** group in
the in-game AddOns list; enable either the release or the dev copies, not both. Run it again after
editing any `.toc`, then restart the game.

All modules share one **Turkey Tickle UI** page in the in-game AddOns options.

## Development

`tests/harness.lua` loads a module in a stubbed WoW environment to catch load and runtime errors
outside the game:

```
luajit tests/harness.lua TurkeyTickleUI_Plates
luajit tests/harness_pets.lua TurkeyTickleUI_Pets
luajit tests/harness_puzzle.lua TurkeyTickleUI_Puzzle [image-code.txt]
luajit tests/harness_cooking.lua TurkeyTickleUI_Cooking
luajit tests/harness_xp.lua TurkeyTickleUI_XP
```

`tests/run_all.sh` runs all of them, then plays the Puzzle module against older releases
(`tests/puzzle_compat.sh`). CI runs it on every push and pull request.

The Pets and Cooking data files are generated from addons in your Forever install:

```
python3 tools/build_pets_data.py
python3 tools/build_cooking_data.py
```

The Puzzle module's image tool is a Rust program in `tools/ttpz`:

```
cargo build --release --manifest-path tools/ttpz/Cargo.toml
tools/ttpz/target/release/ttpz https://example.com/picture.jpg --out /tmp/code.txt
luajit tests/harness_puzzle.lua TurkeyTickleUI_Puzzle /tmp/code.txt
```

## Releasing

All modules share one version, taken from the git tag: plain semver with no `v` (`0.2.0`, or
`0.3.0-beta.1` / `0.3.0-alpha.1` for test builds). The TOCs say `## Version: @project-version@`, and
packaging replaces that with the tag. A copy straight from the repository calls itself `dev`.

Work happens on `main`. To release, push `main` to `prod` (`git push origin main:prod`; the
repository doesn't take pull requests). Every push to `prod` is a release, and the version is picked for you: the patch number
goes up (0.2.0 to 0.2.1), unless a commit title since the last release contains `[minor]`
(0.2.0 to 0.3.0) or `[major]` (0.2.0 to 1.0.0). To release `prod` as it is, or as an exact version
like `0.3.0-beta.1`, run the **Release** workflow on `prod` from the Actions tab. The workflow:

1. Picks the version (`tools/next_version.sh`) and runs `tests/run_all.sh`
2. Tags the commit and writes a changelog from the commits since the last release
3. Packages every module into one zip with the [BigWigs packager](https://github.com/BigWigsMods/packager)
   (`.pkgmeta`) and publishes it as a GitHub release
4. Packages each standalone module (listed in `STANDALONE_MODULES` in
   `.github/workflows/release.yml`, currently just Puzzle) on its own with `tools/package_module.sh`,
   attaches that zip to the release, and uploads it to the module's CurseForge project
5. Attaches the `ttpz` image tool, built for Windows and Linux (`.github/workflows/ttpz.yml`, which
   CI also runs on every push)

CurseForge uploads need a repository secret `CF_API_KEY` (a CurseForge API token). Each standalone
module has its own CurseForge project, set with a repository variable named after it:
`CURSEFORGE_PROJECT_ID_PUZZLE` for Puzzle. A module without that variable only goes to GitHub. The
suite zip with every module goes to GitHub only, unless a `CURSEFORGE_PROJECT_ID` variable is set
for a suite project. Don't put `X-Curse-Project-ID` in the TOCs: the suite packaging would pick it
up and upload everything to that project.

If a Puzzle change needs a new protocol, add the release it will ship in to `PROTOCOL_RELEASES` in
`TurkeyTickleUI_Puzzle/Session.lua` (see the compatibility notes there). The automatic version is
raised to at least that release, and an exact version older than it is refused.

# Turkey Tickle UI 0.2.1

- Add tools/dev_link.sh to run dev copies alongside a release install
- Pets: add a pet guide and family stat modifiers, swing intervals in tooltips and the browser
- Puzzle: open to a list of active puzzles with a host button; rename the rotation option to Piece rotation

# Turkey Tickle UI 0.2.0

- README: release by pushing main to prod
- Only commit titles pick a minor/major release
- Puzzle: own icon on the minimap, windows and AddOns list; keep the icon art
- Release Puzzle standalone for its own CurseForge listing; suite zip stays GitHub-only
- Release from the prod branch with automatic versions
- Puzzle: cut overlapping knobs around each other
- Build ttpz for Windows and Linux in CI and attach it to releases
- CI: use actions/checkout v5 (Node 24)
- Version releases from git tags and package them with GitHub Actions
- Puzzle: turned pieces, join puzzles in progress, puzzle alone, version checks
- ttpz: check Windows certificates against the system store
